t: This is Gladstone Park, about thirty-five hectares of green space in Dollis Hill, in north-west London. It's named after William Ewart Gladstone, the Liberal statesman who served as prime minister four separate times between 1868 and 1894, more than anyone else in that office. He was also Chancellor of the Exchequer four times and sat in Parliament for over sixty years, so his career spanned nearly the whole Victorian era. The park carries his name as a mark of that long public life.
